TRANSFER ADMISSION INFORMATION

You can find information about admission to CSUSB as a transfer student here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students


TRANSFER SUCCESS PATHWAY

Enrolling in the Transfer Success Pathway provides you with dual admission to a California Community College and a specific CSU campus. The TSP ensures a more streamlined transfer experience since you can choose the specific community college courses that will apply to your intended major at your destination CSU campus. See if you qualify for the Transfer Success Pathway here: https://www.calstate.edu/apply/transfer/Pages/transfer-success-pathway.aspx


FINANCIAL AID

Students who plan to transfer directly from a California Community College to a 4-year university can apply for the Cal Grant Transfer Entitlement Award. The application deadline is March 2nd each year, and students must submit a FAFSA or CA Dream Act Application. The minimum GPA is a 2.40. More information is available here: https://www.csac.ca.gov/post/cal-grant-transfer-entitlement-award


ASSOCIATE DEGREES FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

A complete list of CSUSB majors/concentrations that are similar to the Associate Degrees for Transfer (ADTs) can be found here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/associate-degree-transfer

Students who intend to transfer to CSUSB with the ADT guarantee MUST submit final transcripts with the earned ADT recorded by the final document deadline: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students/transfer-deadlines

Students who submit transcripts after the document deadline are NOT guaranteed to graduate within 60 semester units.


EXPLORE MAJORS AND CAREERS

  • The CSUSB Career Center has collected a variety of resources to help students choose or confirm their major and explore different career paths: https://www.csusb.edu/career-center/students/career-resources/major-and-career-exploration


TEST CREDIT

Do you have questions about your transfer work? Need some guidance? You can talk with one of our Transfer and Graduation Counselors!

  • Email: transferhelp@csusb.edu
  • Phone: 909-537-5200, Option 4
  • Zoom: Set up an appointment by emailing transferhelp@csusb.edu

You are also welcome to visit us in person. We are located in the Office of the Registrar, on the first floor of University Hall (interactive map link).

CONCENTRATIONS

Students in this major are required to choose one of the following concentrations:

  • Biochemistry
  • Chemistry


MAJOR INFORMATION

The Bachelor's of Art degree program in chemistry is designed for the student who plans a career in chemistry or the related sciences upon graduation, continuation to graduate school in the chemical sciences, or professional health sciences such as medicine or pharmacy, but is interested in studying other subjects to augment a basic chemistry curriculum, perhaps with a minor or a double major in another field, for example. The program provides foundational course work in the sub-disciplinary areas of organic, inorganic, physical, analytical, and biochemistry with cognate course work in biology, mathematics and physics. A concentration in biochemistry or chemistry is required. The B.A. program is not certified by the American Chemical Society.


The B.A. in Chemistry provides additional chemistry electives and fewer requirements than the B.S. degree program. The Chemistry concentration may be an appropriate degree for those that would like to become high school chemistry teachers, for example. The Biochemistry option requires biology and biochemistry course and laboratory work, and may be more appropriate for students interested in the biotech industry, medical or pharmacy school, or clinical laboratory science.


The Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry at CSUSB offers four degree programs: BS – Chemistry Concentration; BS – Biochemistry Concentration; BA – Chemistry Concentration; BA – Biochemistry Concentration. Both BS degrees are certified by the American Chemical Society. We graduate between 30 and 50+ students each year, with about half of our graduates starting their studies at regional community colleges. Most classes are deliberately kept to a moderate size, so students can better interact with the instructor and learn actively. Upper division classes are anywhere between 10-60 students, and upper division laboratory classes, which are taught primarily by permanent faculty members, enroll between 12-20 students. Chemistry majors are assigned a faculty advisor who is available to provide advice. In addition to taking the usual complement of coursework, students may also carry out independent research projects in association with one of the faculty members; about half of our majors undertake research projects or internships, and all B.S. major students are required to have a course-based and/or independent research experience. Our majors pursue a variety of post-graduation pathways, including graduate study in chemistry/biochemistry (M.S. and Ph.D.), professional programs in pharmacy or medicine, employment in laboratories in government or private industry, and secondary school teaching.

**ARTICULATES AS A SERIES ONLY: If this description appears next to a requirement below, please refer to the Department Articulation Agreement for that course for more information. It typically means that an exact articulation to the CSUSB requirement is not possible.


This major expects that all laboratory courses required for the major will be completed in-person. The upper-division coursework assumes that students have broad experience conducting in-person lab work.

ASSOCIATE DEGREE FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

The Chemistry Concentration is similar to the Associate Degree for Transfer (ADT) in Chemistry (the Biochemistry Concentration is not similar).

﻿HOWEVER, the articulation agreement below represents the straightest pathway through the major.

Completion of the ADT guarantees that students will be able to graduate from a similar-designated major at CSUSB in no more than 60 semester units. The ADT does not guarantee that all lower-division requirements are met.


Community college transfer students with a compatible ADT MUST meet with an academic advisor early in their first term and each subsequent term to stay on track for graduation.
